subject: mathematics
question_text: If A + B + C = 3π/2, prove that cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C = 1 − 4 sin A sin B sin C.

mark_split.label: Convert sin C inside the bracket
Apply the difference formula and conclude

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), the TRANSFORMATIONS banner (the book prints TRANSFORMATIONS as a separate un-numbered chapter-style banner immediately after chapter 8's VSAQ run, and restarts its numbering at 1 — we ship both under one unit, ordered by the syllabus, and never mirror the book's arrangement), Long Answer question 7(i), book p.102. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives its two two-mark blocks to the pairing and to the substitution cos(3π/2 − C) = −sin C, because that minus sign is where this question is actually lost; the remaining moves are one mark each. THE CONDITION IS 3π/2, NOT π AND NOT π/2, AND THAT DECIDES TWO SIGNS: A + B = 3π/2 − C gives cos(A+B) = −sin C, and C = 3π/2 − (A+B) gives sin C = −cos(A+B). Both minus signs are needed, and they are what turn the π/2 version's answer (1 + 4 sin A sin B sin C) into this one (1 − 4 sin A sin B sin C). A student who substitutes A + B = π − C here gets the wrong sign twice. NUMERIC CHECK (before authoring and again after): at A = 100°, B = 80°, C = 90°, which sums to 270°, L.H.S = −2.8793852416 and R.H.S = −2.8793852416; re-checked on a second, non-right-angled witness A = 110°, B = 95°, C = 65°, where both sides equal −2.3936398058. The printed identity is correct as stated. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C prints 3 long answers and the student answers any 2, at 8 marks each (2026-27 pattern). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A and Maths-2B expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this identity — name each move in order, and say what the 3π/2 condition does to the signs.

steps.label: State the 3π/2 condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. The condition here is 3π/2. It is used twice below and it puts a minus sign on BOTH substitutions.
steps.memory_tip: The sum is 3π/2 here. This condition puts a minus sign on both substitutions, and that minus is the whole difference from the π/2 version.
lines: (So A, B, C are not the angles of a triangle;

recall.must_convey: That the condition is A + B + C = 3π/2 and it is rearranged to A + B = 3π/2 − C.

steps.why: The statement is false without the condition and false with the wrong one. Writing A + B = 3π/2 − C now fixes the sign of both substitutions below.
common_mistakes: Using A + B = π − C, the triangle condition, which gives cos(A+B) = −cos C where −sin C is needed.
Starting the transformation before writing the condition.

steps.label: Pair the first two cosines
steps.margin_note: Two of the eight marks. cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2), applied to cos 2A + cos 2B. The 2s inside cancel the halves.
steps.memory_tip: Pair the first two only. The halves in the formula cancel the 2s in cos 2A and cos 2B.

lines.text: Use the sum formula with p = 2A, q = 2B:
\dfrac{p + q}{2} = \ A\ + \ B\ \text{and}\ \dfrac{p - q}{2} = \ A\ - \ B

recall.must_convey: That cos 2A + cos 2B becomes 2 cos(A+B) cos(A−B).
accept: group the first two and apply cos C plus cos D to get two cos of A plus B into cos of A minus B
the halves cancel leaving A plus B and A minus B
apply the sum to product formula to the first two terms
modati rendu group chesi sum to product apply cheyyali
convert the first pair into a product

steps.why: The 2s inside cos 2A and cos 2B are halved by the formula, so the double angles become plain A + B and A − B, and A + B is what the condition can replace.
common_mistakes: Pairing cos 2B with cos 2C and then forgetting that B + C = 3π/2 − A, so that cos(B + C) = −sin A.
Forgetting to halve the sum and the difference.

steps.label: Use the condition
steps.margin_note: Two marks, and the sign here decides the whole answer. cos(3π/2 − θ) = −sin θ, so a minus sign enters the expression.
steps.memory_tip: cos(3π/2 − θ) = −sin θ. The MINUS is what makes the answer 1 − 4 sin A sin B sin C instead of 1 + 4 sin A sin B sin C.

lines.text: Change cos(A+B) using the given sum:
(3π/2 is an odd multiple of π/2, so cos becomes
sin; 3π/2 − θ is in Q₃, where cos is negative)

recall.must_convey: That cos(A+B) = cos(3π/2 − C) = −sin C, with the minus sign.
accept: cos of three pi by two minus C is minus sin C
the cosine becomes a negative sine under the three pi by two shift
use the condition and keep the minus sign
cos three pi by two minus C ante minus sin C
apply the angle condition, it gives minus sin C
heard_as: three pi by two minus C

steps.why: 3π/2 − θ lands in the third quadrant, where cosine is negative, so the shift carries a minus sign. That single sign separates this question from the π/2 version.
common_mistakes: Writing cos(3π/2 − C) = +sin C and losing the minus.
Writing cos(3π/2 − C) = −cos C, which mixes up the shift.

steps.label: Expand cos 2C
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. cos 2θ has three forms; only 1 − 2 sin²θ leaves a standalone 1, which is the first term on the right-hand side.
steps.memory_tip: Choose cos 2C = 1 − 2 sin²C out of the three forms — it is the one that produces the 1 on the right.

recall.must_convey: That cos 2C = 1 − 2 sin²C is chosen, and 2 sin C is factored out of the remaining two terms.
accept: cos two C is one minus two sin squared C and then take two sin C common
use the form of cos two theta that gives a one
the one on the right comes straight from the double angle formula
cos two C ni one minus two sin square C ga rasi two sin C common teeyali
expand the double angle and factor

steps.why: The right-hand side opens with a 1, so a 1 has to be manufactured. Of the three forms of cos 2θ only 1 − 2 sin²θ leaves one standing on its own.
common_mistakes: Using cos 2C = 2 cos²C − 1, which produces cosines where the right-hand side carries sines.

steps.label: Convert sin C inside the bracket
steps.margin_note: Seventh mark. The condition is used a SECOND time, and it carries a minus sign again: sin(3π/2 − θ) = −cos θ. That turns the bracket into a DIFFERENCE of cosines.
steps.memory_tip: sin(3π/2 − θ) = −cos θ. The second minus turns the plus inside the bracket into a minus.

lines.text: Write sinC in terms of A + B:

recall.must_convey: That sin C inside the bracket equals −cos(A+B), so the bracket becomes cos(A−B) − cos(A+B).
accept: sin C is minus cos of A plus B so the bracket becomes a difference of cosines
use the condition again on the inside sin C and keep the minus
the plus inside the bracket turns into a minus
bracket lo sin C ni minus cos A plus B ga marchali
sin three pi by two minus theta is minus cos theta

steps.why: The sin C outside stays; only the one inside converts. It converts to −cos(A+B), and that minus is what makes the bracket a difference the product formula can close.
common_mistakes: Converting both sin C terms instead of only the inside one.
Writing sin(3π/2 − θ) = +cos θ, which leaves the bracket as a sum.

steps.label: Apply the difference formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos(A−B) − cos(A+B) = 2 sin A sin B closes the proof. Write "= R.H.S" so the examiner can see the last line reaches the right-hand side.
steps.memory_tip: cos(A−B) − cos(A+B) = 2 sin A sin B. The two 2s multiply to give the 4.

lines.text: (expand both; the cosA cosB terms cancel)

recall.must_convey: That cos(A−B) − cos(A+B) = 2 sin A sin B, giving 1 − 4 sin A sin B sin C.
accept: cos A minus B minus cos A plus B is two sin A sin B so the answer is one minus four sin A sin B sin C
the bracket becomes two sin A sin B and the two twos give four
apply the cosine difference formula to finish
bracket lo two sin A sin B vasthundi, rendu twos kalisi four
the final answer is one minus four sin A sin B sin C
heard_as: sin A sin B sin C

steps.why: A difference of two cosines is a product of two sines. The 4 comes from the 2 taken out in step 4 times the 2 this formula supplies, and the leading 1 is already in place.
common_mistakes: Using cos(A+B) − cos(A−B), which reverses the sign.
Dropping the leading 1 while writing the final line.
